eosrs.note: The satellite map is preliminary and less reliable over built-up and vegetated ground.

gates.gate: Better than UP NOAH's map on its own
gates.detail: AUC gain 0.028 (95% interval -0.008 to 0.068); Boyce gain -0.084 (-0.210 to 0.103), shown only. Judged on AUC: UP NOAH's map has only four levels, which a continuous Boyce index cannot compare fairly with a continuous score.

gates.gate: GeoAlert Mananga flood points in Red or Orange
Red and Orange cover at most half the buildings

gates.detail: The choice and the cut-offs were fixed before any test point was loaded.

reasons: It did not clearly beat UP NOAH's map on its own: the lower end of its AUC gain was -0.008, not above zero.
Red and Orange would cover 71% of the floodplain's buildings, more than half.

fallback.note: UP NOAH's map missed about a third of the survey's flood spots. It flags about 57% of the assessed buildings as Red or Orange, more than the half the machine-learning model was allowed.

basis: From UP NOAH's 25-year flood model, classed by where floods reached in the 2017 UP Mananga flood survey. It shows how flood-prone an area is, not whether a flood is coming, and it is the same in every month.
limits: The survey points are places where residents remembered floods (typhoons of 1990-2014). The other buildings are not known to be dry, so the levels show how flood-prone an area is compared with the rest, not a chance of flooding.
Every survey point lies along the lower Mananga River, so areas away from it are not assessed.
The Mananga River works planned for 2026 may change where floods reach; the model learned from the river before them.
UP NOAH's flood maps are labelled beta.
This is not a forecast: it is the same in every month and does not say a flood is coming.
